precepts.text: The days come when it shall no more be said the Most High liveth that brought Israel out of Egypt, but that brought them from the land of the north, which is North America.
precepts.point: David will speak of the glorious honor of His majesty and His terrible acts and declare His greatness. When the kingdom comes we will have something new to talk about, no longer only the deliverance of the past.

note.label: Psalm 145: The Greatness and Mercy of the Most High

precepts.why:
“One generation shall praise thy works to another, and shall declare thy mighty acts.” When the kingdom comes we will have something new to talk about, no longer only the deliverance of the past: “it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt; But, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north, and from all the lands whither he had driven them: and I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.”

The land of the north is North America. That is the mighty act the next generation will declare.

precepts.text: Judah and Israel were oppressed together, pressed together right here in Babylon, in America.
precepts.point: David will speak of the glorious honor of His majesty and His terrible acts and declare His greatness. When the kingdom comes we will have something new to talk about, no longer only the deliverance of the past.

note.label: Psalm 145: The Greatness and Mercy of the Most High

precepts.why: “The children of Israel and the children of Judah were oppressed together: and all that took them captives held them fast; they refused to let them go.” Judah and Israel were oppressed together, pressed together right here in Babylon, in America. The deliverance from this oppression is the terrible act and the greatness one generation will declare to another.

precepts.text: The Most High will set His hand again to recover His people from all the places He scattered them.
precepts.point: David will speak of the glorious honor of His majesty and His terrible acts and declare His greatness. When the kingdom comes we will have something new to talk about, no longer only the deliverance of the past.

note.label: Psalm 145: The Greatness and Mercy of the Most High

precepts.why: “the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.” The Most High will set his hand again to recover his people from all the places he scattered them. That second recovery is the new thing we will speak of, the glorious honour of his majesty and his wondrous works declared to the generation to come.

precepts.text: Through Christ the forgiveness of sins is preached, and all who believe are justified from things the law of Moses could not justify, since some sins in that law required our blood.
precepts.point: His compassion and mercy is another word for grace. He is good to all, and His tender mercies are over all His works.

note.label: Psalm 145: The Greatness and Mercy of the Most High

precepts.why:
“The Lord is gracious, and full of compassion; slow to anger, and of great mercy.” His compassion and mercy is another word for grace. “Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins: And by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.”

Through Christ the forgiveness of sins is preached, and all who believe are justified from things the law of Moses could not justify, since some sins in that law required our blood. That is the great goodness they shall abundantly utter the memory of.

precepts.text: God is a spirit, and they that worship Him must worship Him in spirit and in truth.
precepts.point: He is near to all who call upon Him in truth. Calling upon Him in truth means keeping His commandments.

note.label: Psalm 145: The Greatness and Mercy of the Most High

precepts.why: “The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth.” “God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.” Calling upon him in truth is worshipping him in truth, and that means keeping his commandments.

precepts.text: His law is the truth, so we must worship Him according to the commandments.
precepts.point: He is near to all who call upon Him in truth. Calling upon Him in truth means keeping His commandments.

note.label: Psalm 145: The Greatness and Mercy of the Most High

precepts.why: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” His law is the truth, so calling upon him in truth means keeping his commandments; we must worship him according to the commandments. He is righteous in all his ways and holy in all his works, and he is nigh to those who call on him that way.

precepts.text: This is the love of God, that we keep His commandments.
precepts.point: The Most High preserves all that love Him but destroys the wicked; loving Him means keeping His commandments.

note.label: Psalm 145: The Greatness and Mercy of the Most High

precepts.why: “The Lord preserveth all them that love him: but all the wicked will he destroy.” Loving him means keeping his commandments: “For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.” He fulfills the desire of them that fear him, hears their cry, and saves them, and those he preserves are those who love him by keeping his commandments.
